title: Preemie milestones — corrected age matters
summary: Babies born early often reach skills on a adjusted timeline. That is expected.
whatsNormal:
Corrected (adjusted) age counts from the due date, not the birth date.

• Example: born 8 weeks early, now 4 months old by birth date → corrected age about 2 months
• Many preemies catch up to peers by age 2–3 for large motor skills; smaller differences can persist
• Use corrected age for milestone guides until at least age 2 (your pediatrician may adjust)
• NICU graduates may have extra follow-up for vision, hearing, and development

Celebrate progress without comparing to full-term babies of the same birth age.
watchFor: Not fixing and following faces by corrected 2–3 months
Very stiff or very floppy muscle tone
No social smiles by corrected 3 months
Feeding difficulty worsening after NICU discharge
callDoctorIf: Regression — skills your baby had are lost
You want early intervention referral — ask at any visit; earlier support helps
Your NICU or developmental follow-up clinic gave specific checklists — use those dates
